jobs.title: The unit suite must be green under a scratch TMPDIR, not only the real one
jobs.bodyPreview:
# Goal

After ss-07 (PRD 1267, commit 7ac7259) the unit suite is fully green with the real TMPDIR (473/473 files, 4620 tests) but reproducibly red — twice, same two failures — under `TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)`, which is the exact invocation every ss-* PRD gate prescribes: opsErrorLogTelemetryTap "an ephemeral cwd yields zero local lines but one telemetry record" and prdLocationsArchived "a prds-archived/ dir created inside an ALREADY-EXISTING Epic is bounded-stale". Neither file was touched by ss-07; both derive fixtures from os.tmpdir(), which the override moves out from under the sandbox globalSetup's own mkdtemp. Make the suite green in BOTH TMPDIR modes so the standing gate command stops reporting a false red on every future PRD.

jobs.title: Route the remaining scheduler-owned home paths through schedulerPaths
jobs.bodyPreview:
# Goal

ss-05 (PRD 1264, commit bcdb335) landed schedulerPaths.cjs and routed all eight modules it enumerated, but its own clean-case command still exits 1: nine scheduler-owned home-rooted paths outside that list remain module-scope consts computed from os.homedir() at require time. A test or second instance that sets SM_SCHEDULER_HOME therefore still writes the LIVE audit log, history rollup, scheduled-plans history, instance lock, procname aliases and heap-snapshot dir — exactly the half-redirect ss-05 exists to prevent. Route them through the resolver (adding the few missing exports) so SM_SCHEDULER_HOME redirects every scheduler-owned path, and make the clean-case command pass.

jobs.title: Worktree roots resolve through schedulerPaths too (SM_WORKTREE_ROOT), including the ephemeral-cwd definition and the tmpdir guard
jobs.bodyPreview:
# Goal

The job and epic worktree roots are hardcoded under os.tmpdir() in gitWorktree.cjs KIND_CONFIG, snapshotted at module load by ephemeralCwd.cjs (MANAGED_WORKTREE_ROOTS) and guarded by removeWorktreeDir's `parentDir === os.tmpdir()` check. HOME overrides never reach them, which is why the unit suite can sweep the LIVE job-worktree root. Make both roots move as a unit under one override.

jobs.title: usage.cjs: one in-flight request, one shared result for the renderer IPC path and the scheduler pollLoop
jobs.bodyPreview:
# Goal

Two independent callers hit the usage meter with one OAuth token: the renderer through the billing:fetch IPC handler (which alone owns the 30 s OK cache and ~/.claude/session-manager/billing-cache.json) and the scheduler through pollLoop, which never reads that cache. A success on one path never resets the other's failure streak (on 2026-09-13 the renderer got an ok at 1:10 PM PDT while the scheduler's streak ran through it unbroken), and both request streams add up against an endpoint that rate-limits the caller. Make fetchUsage the single owner of caching, single-flight de-duplication and Retry-After.

# Acceptance criteria

jobs.title: Repair and prove the install upsert: app_installs never receives a record from this machine
jobs.bodyPreview:
# Goal

Every install-shaped number on bilko.run's usage endpoint (`GET /api/admin/session-manager/usage`: total/active7/active30/new7, installs-by-version, installs-by-platform, install specs) reads from the `app_installs` table, which is populated only by `POST /api/telemetry/install` — and this machine has never sent one. Evidence: `~/.config/session-manager/telemetry.json` on the running 0.85.0 npx build still holds `lastMachineReportAt: null` and `lastMachineReportVersion: ""` (so `isMachineReportDue()` is true and has stayed true across boots), no `install`-channel record appears in the queue spool while 2,195 `event`/`log`/`error` records went through it, and no `bootSequence failed` warn line was logged. The live ingest route is healthy (an empty POST returns `400 install_id_required`), so this is a client-side failure, not a server one. Find the actual break in the boot path and make the failure impossible to have again silently.

# Acceptance criteria
